anti_overlap: Does not evaluate the abstract falsifiability of the influence→principle→rule citation mechanism — that is fd-designsystems-token-contract-rigor.
Does not cover color contrast, CVD-safety, dark-mode color science, or typographic legibility science — that is fd-typography-color-accessibility-science.
Scoped to motion, interaction states (loading/error/empty/offline), responsive layout, and i18n/RTL — the states and contexts a happy-path canon tends to omit.
decision_lens: Take the canon's happy-path rules (holdover, tempo, one-gesture act, here/there) and ask what each one says about loading, error, empty, offline, slow-network, reduced-motion, and non-LTR conditions — then flag every case where the answer is 'nothing.'
focus: Motion/interaction design rigor and state-space completeness: whether the canon's OODA/holdover/tempo claims translate into an actual motion system, and whether the load-bearing states every real product needs (loading, empty, error, offline, responsive breakpoints, i18n/RTL) are addressed at all
name: fd-interaction-statespace-completeness
persona: Apply the perspective of an interaction and motion-design systems lead who has built the animation/state layer for production design systems (transition curves, reduced-motion fallbacks, skeleton/loading/error/empty states, responsive and internationalization contracts) and treats a design canon's silence on these as more dangerous than an explicit wrong answer, because silence means every component team invents its own — this reviewer measures success by asking 'if I had to ship a real screen with a network failure, an empty result set, a slow connection, and a right-to-left locale, does this canon tell me anything at all,' and is alert to canons that read as complete because they're eloquent about the happy path while never mentioning the states that dominate real usage.
review_areas: Motion is asserted as load-bearing ('holdover, not jump-cut,' §9; 'tempo over completeness,' §10) but the canon specifies zero actual motion values — no easing curves, no duration tokens, no distinction between the reticle's 'tracking' animation and any other transition, and critically no `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback is mentioned anywhere despite motion being explicitly named as one of the four token categories in the roadmap; a canon that names 'tracks, never teleports' as signature behavior owes an accessible-motion story, and has none.

Loading states are addressed only obliquely via OODA(RC) §10 ('a fast, oriented, slightly-incomplete render beats a slow, exhaustive one') which describes a philosophy of graceful degradation but specifies no actual skeleton/placeholder pattern, no stated maximum acceptable latency, and no treatment of what 'slightly incomplete' looks like visually (partial route line? grayed stat strip? spinner, which would violate the calm/precision aesthetic?) — every other rule in the canon reaches implementation detail (exact hex, exact font stack) except this one, which is exactly the state every route computation will pass through.

Error states are entirely absent from all ten principle sets: no rule addresses what happens when routing fails, when the shadow raster has no coverage for a location, when the network is offline, or when GPS/location permission is denied — for a system whose central metaphor is 'orient before decide' (OODA §10), the failure to orient (no data, no signal, no permission) is the single most important edge case to give a principled answer to, and the canon is silent.

Empty states are unaddressed: what does the map look like before a destination is picked, what does the StatStrip show before a route exists, what does 'here' look like with no 'there' yet (directly relevant to Meyrowitz §3's here/there framing, which describes the two-state relationship but never the zero-state) — this is a gap in exactly the principle that should have covered it.

Responsive/viewport behavior is entirely unaddressed despite the canon explicitly claiming PWA/installable ambitions elsewhere in project docs — no rule states how the closed-vocabulary fixed-position components (§6, 'system-as-garment... fixed set of panels in fixed positions') behave when a small phone viewport cannot fit the fixed positions, which directly threatens the 'the walker learns the garment once and wears it everywhere' promise if the garment must be resewn per breakpoint with no guidance.

Internationalization/RTL and variable-length content are unaddressed: the Ong-derived two-register typography (§4) and the inscribed serif for place names/felt-minutes assumes Latin-script, LTR, and a certain numeral-and-label density — there is no statement about how the register distinction or the fixed-position component vocabulary survives a right-to-left locale, CJK place names, or a felt-minutes/distance format that's wider in another language, despite Solwend being a walking app in a category (maps/routing) where internationalization is close to inevitable.

severity_examples.condition: OODA(RC) makes 'orient before decide' the system's core interaction loop, but when orientation data itself fails (no shade raster coverage, GPS denied, offline), the canon gives zero guidance on how the system should render its own failure to orient — the most philosophically important edge case in the entire canon (what does the interface do when it cannot orient the walker) is the one case none of the ten influences was spent on.
severity_examples.scenario: No error-state principle in a system whose founding metaphor is orientation before decision

severity_examples.condition: The token roadmap lists motion (holdover/tempo) as one of four token categories to build, but the canon that's supposed to constrain it gives no duration/easing values and never mentions `prefers-reduced-motion`; the first component author to build the reticle's tracking animation has to invent both the actual motion curve and the accessibility fallback from scratch, with no citation possible back to canon — violating the canon's own stated rule that 'every token cites a rule.'
severity_examples.scenario: Motion named as a token category with zero specified values and no reduced-motion fallback

severity_examples.condition: ACRONYM's system-as-garment principle promises a walker 'learns the garment once and wears it everywhere,' but with no responsive rule, a small-viewport build either breaks the fixed-position promise (panels move/collapse, contradicting §6) or overflows/clips content (violating legibility) — and the canon offers no way to decide which failure is more acceptable.
severity_examples.scenario: Fixed-position 'system-as-garment' vocabulary has no responsive contract

severity_examples.condition: Without a stated loading pattern, an implementer reaches for a generic spinner — which is exactly the kind of 'decoration that reads as nothing' the canon elsewhere forbids (§6, 'every element earns its place') — creating a component that violates the canon's own ornament rule the moment it handles the single state every route request passes through before resolving.
severity_examples.scenario: Loading state has no visual spec and risks contradicting the calm-precision aesthetic

success_hints: Recommend the canon add an eleventh consideration (or fold into OODA §10) that explicitly addresses failure-to-orient states: no-data, offline, permission-denied, each with a stated visual treatment consistent with the calm/instrument aesthetic (e.g., 'the reticle idles' rather than a generic spinner).

Require the motion token category to inherit an explicit accessible-motion rule (`prefers-reduced-motion` support, stated max/min durations) before any component ships a holdover animation, since motion is named as canon-derived but currently has no canon content to derive from.
Add an explicit empty-state rule under Meyrowitz (§3) since here/there is the natural home for 'here with no there yet' — this closes a gap in the exact principle already positioned to own it.

Flag responsive/viewport and i18n/RTL as open canon gaps that must be resolved before the component library (item 3 in 'Next in the sequence') begins, since the system-as-garment fixed-position promise cannot be kept without a stated breakpoint and locale contract.
task_context: Adversarially and creatively stress-test the Shadewright design-system canon: find internal contradictions between the 10 principle sets; rules that are vibes rather than falsifiable contracts; missing load-bearing concerns (accessibility, dark mode, motion, responsive, i18n, error/empty/loading states); places where the influence→principle→rule chain fails to actually constrain token or component design; and creative blind spots — what a great design-system canon would have that this one lacks.
